Done. Reflection complete and the lesson is saved.

What went wrong and what I saved:

The error — I read the TSO-3 "Treasury Bills: Regular weekly and annual maturing" rows, whose "Total amount outstanding" cells are par values of bills MATURING in each month (a maturity-distribution table, values decaying 20k-31k → ~3k), and counted the 7 that exceeded $20,000M. The question asked for total nominal bills OUTSTANDING (the stock), which is the grand-total line (~$164,005M Jan 1977 / $161,221M Jan 1978) — far above $20,000M every month. With each survey standing in for its 12 forward months, the gold answer is 12.

Saved to: `references/ownership-survey-and-count-threshold.md` (new "MATURITY-DISTRIBUTION TRAP" section) plus a strengthened pointer in SKILL.md so the ref loads for this question shape.

Generalizable rule recorded: "total ... outstanding" of a security type = its TOTAL / grand-total line in TSO-2 or the "Total <type>" line in TSO-3 — never the individual issue/maturity-month rows. Read by-issue/by-maturity rows ONLY when the question names a specific coupon or maturity date. The decay signature (large → ~3k down a 12-month column) is the tell that a table is maturity buckets, not a stock time series.

Memory is at capacity (2,152/2,200), so I kept the procedural depth in the linked reference file rather than evicting an existing high-value entry; the skill pointer guarantees it loads next time.
